§ 3GANDHIAN ERA

§ 4MAHATMA GANDHI

  • Full name: Mohan Das Karamchand Gandhi
  • Birth: 2nd October 1869 in Porbandar, Gujarat
  • Mother: Putlibai Gandhi
  • Father: Karamchand Gandhi

§ 5Gandhi's Work in South Africa

  • He setup Natal Indian Congress (1894) in South Africa against the racial discrimination carried out towards the Indians and South Africans.
  • He started Indian Opinion Newspaper (1903).
  • He also setup Phoenix Farm (1904) and Tolstoy Farm (1910).
  • Gandhi was involved in Satyagraha against Registration of Marriage Act.
  • He also led a campaign against the restriction of Indian migration and recognition of Hindu marriages that were not recognised in South Africa.

§ 6Gandhi in India

  • Gandhi returned to India on 9 Jan 1915 which is celebrated as Pravasiya Bhartiya Diwas for Non-Resident Indians (NRI).
  • Political Guru: Gopal Krishna Gokhale
  • His first public appearance was at Banaras Hindu University (BHU) inauguration in 1916.
  • BHU was founded by Madan Mohan Malaviya. He also founded Hindu Mahasabha (1915)
  • Book written by Gandhi: Hind Swaraj (also known as Indian Home Rule, where he wrote that "the British rule in India was a result of cooperation extended by Indians")

Autobiography of Mahatma Gandhi: The Story of My Experiments with Truth

§ 7Movements Led by Gandhiji

  1. 1. Champaran Satyagrah (1917) → First Civil Disobedience Movement
  • Raj Kumar Shukla invited Gandhi to Champaran, Bihar to complain about injustice of the landlord system where the farmers were forced to cultivate Indigo in 3/20th part of their land, also known as Tinkathia System.
  • Other people involved in Champaran Satyagraha: Rajendra Prasad, Mazhar-ul-Haq, J. B. Kriplani

§ 8Champaran Agrarian Act (1918)

  • This act was a direct result of Champaran Satyagraha. It abolished Tinkathia system and suspended Abwab tax (an illegal collection imposed by landlords on peasants).
  1. 2. Ahmedabad Mill Strike (1918) → First Hunger Strike
  • Anusuya Sarabhai invited Gandhi to Ahmedabad where textile workers of mill in Ahmedabad fought for economic injustice when the mill owners discontinued their Plague Bonus.
  • Workers demanded a 50% wage hike to compensate for rising costs of living. The mill owners offered only a 20% raise which led to the strike. Finally wage hike was settled at 35%.
  1. 3. Kheda Satyagrah (1918) → First Non-Cooperation
  • This Satyagraha movement was carried out at Kheda district of Gujarat in support of the peasants who were not able to pay the land tax due to the failure of crops.

§ 9GOVERNMENT OF INDIA ACT (1919)

  • It is also known as Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms.
  • Montagu was the Secretary and Chelmsford was the Viceroy.
  • Provisions made:
  1. 1. It extended separate electorate to Anglo Indians, Christians.
  2. 2. It introduced dyarchy at provinces → Provincial subjects were divided into two parts.
ReservedTransferred
It was administrated by the Governor through his Executive Council.It was administrated by Ministers from Legislative Council.
Eg: Land revenue, Police, FinanceEg: Agriculture, Health, Education
  1. 3. It introduced Bicameral Legislature at Centre.

§ 10ROWLATT SATYAGRAHA (1919)

  • The Rowlatt Satyagraha was a non-violent protest movement led by Mahatma Gandhi against the Rowlatt Act (1919), which was passed by the British government to curb revolutionary activities in India. He called this Act the "Black Act", the act sought to suspend the law of Habeas Corpus, which protects a person's right against unlawful detention.

§ 11Background of Rowlatt Act

  • It was suggested by Sydney Rowlatt (a British Judge).
  • It was officially called the Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act, 1919.
  • It allowed the British government to detain people without trial and imprison them for 2 years without trial.
  • It is an extension of the Defence of India Act, 1915, a World War I time law, even though the World War I had already ended.

§ 12Jallianwala Bagh Massacre 1919

  • It took place on 13 April 1919 (on Baisakhi).
  • In Jallianwala Bagh, Amritsar people gathered in mass for two reasons: To celebrate Baisakhi and to protest against the arrest of Saifuddin Kitchlew and Dr. Satyapal.
  • Without warning, Brigadier General Reginald Dyer, accompanied by his armed troops, closed the only exit gate and open fired at the crowd.

§ 13Aftermath of Jallianwala Bagh Massacre

  • Rabindranath Tagore returned his "Knighthood".
  • Mahatma Gandhi returned his title of "Kaisar-i-Hind" that he received for his work during Boer Wars in South Africa.
  • Hunter Commission was setup to investigate the actions of Reginald Dyer but it did not impose any penal action → Indemnity Act was passed by the British Parliament to protect him.
  • The British Elites started "Morning Post" (a fund collection) in support of Dyer. (Rudyard Kipling also funded in this)
  • Arur Singh (clergy in Golden Temple) titled Reginald Dyer as "Sikh" due to which Gurudwara Reform Movement was launched later in 1920 to free the Gurudwaras from corrupt Mahants.
  • Udham Singh killed Michael O'Dyer (Lieutenant Governor of Punjab during Jallianwala Bagh Massacre who supported "Reginald Dyer") using name "Ram Mohammed Singh Azad" in 1940.

§ 14KHILAFAT MOVEMENT (1919)

  • It was launched after World War I.
  • When World War I ended, Britishers removed Khalifa in Turkey from power. This instigated Muslims all over the world, and Khilafat movement was its response in India.
  • An All India Khilafat Committee was setup in Bombay on March 1919, under the leadership of Ali Brothers (Maulana Ali and Shaukat Ali), Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, Hasrat Mohani, Ajmal Khan.
  • All India Khilafat Conference was held in Delhi on 23 Nov 1919 that was headed by Mahatma Gandhi (the President of the Conference). Note: B G Tilak was initially sceptical of an alliance with Muslim leaders on a religious issue, but the broader Congress eventually endorsed the Khilafat cause and merged it with the Non-Cooperation Movement.

Indian National Liberation Federation formed by: Surendranath Banerjee

§ 15NON-COOPERATION MOVEMENT (1920)

  • It was launched in 1920.
  • Non Cooperation Movement was approved in a special session of Congress held at Calcutta in 1920 and later endorsed in Nagpur in the annual session. It also led to the formation of 15-membered Congress Working Committee.
  • Congress committed itself to extra-constitution mass struggle from now onwards. Jinnah, Annie Besant, B C Pal left the Congress due to ideological differences.
  • Gandhi merged Khilafat Movement with it to ensure Hindu-Muslim unity.
  • 1921: Tilak Swaraj Fund in remembrance of B G Tilak was setup.
  • Local struggles:
  • Eka Movement (1921 in Uttar Pradesh, led by Madari Pasi)
  • Mappila/Malabar/Moplah Revolt (1921): The Uprising was mainly led by Muslim peasants against Hindu feudal lords in the Malabar region of Kerala.
  • Sikh agitation for removal of corrupt Mahants.
  • Awadh Kisan Movement: A peasant movement also started to oppose British rule. Awadh Kisan Sabha was organised by Baba Ramchandra in 1920.

§ 16Steps Taken to Support the Merger of Khilafat Movement and Non-Cooperation Movement

  • On National-level, educational institutions were established as part of boycott of British-run schools and colleges, institutions such as Jamia Millia Islam, Kashi Vidhyapith, Bihar Vidhyapith.
  • Fundraising for the Movement: A significant amount of Rs1 Crore was raised, which was utilised to:
  • Promote national education.
  • Organise protest and strikes.
  • Support the boycott movement.

§ 17Chauri Chaura Incident (1922)

  • On 4th Feb 1922, the crowd of non-cooperation movement burnt a police station in Chauri Chaura a village in Gorakhpur, in which 22 policemen died.
  • As a result, Gandhi called off the non-cooperation movement due to violence and was later jailed in March 1922.

§ 18Suspension of the Movement and Political Vacuum

  • In Bardoli, Congress working committee suspended the non-cooperation movement due to violence and focused on constructive work from now onwards.
  • This led to a political vacuum within the Congress party, as leaders were divided on what to do next.

The division created two groups:

  • No Changers: This group, led by Rajendra Prasad, Vallabhbhai Patel, and M.A. Ansari, believed in continuing Gandhi's principles. They boycotted the British councils and instead focused on constructive work like setting up ashrams, schools, and promoting Khadi (hand-spun cloth).
  • Pro Changers: It was led by C.R. Das, Motilal Nehru, and Ajmal Khan, this group argued that entering the legislative councils would allow them to challenge British rule from within by opposing unfair laws and policies. However, Gandhi initially opposed this idea, as he felt cooperating with the British in any form would weaken the freedom struggle.

§ 19FORMATION OF SWARAJ PARTY, 1923

  • In the Gaya Session of Congress (Dec 1922), the Pro Changers decided to form their own political party the 'Congress Khilafat Swaraj Party' or 'Swaraj Party'.
  • Leadership: C.R. Das → President; Motilal Nehru → Secretary.
  • Goal: "To end or mend the Council".
  • Achievement: Successfully defeated the "Public Safety Bill" in 1928.

Chittaranjan Das (C. R. Das) is also known by the name of "Deshbandhu".

§ 20Belgaum Session of Congress, 1924

  • It was presided by Gandhi (it is the only session presided by him).
  • This session accepted the Swaraj party within the Congress.
